subject: Marketplace nexus / invoicing handshake for GreenPeak co-sell
messages:

Cc: liam.chen@aws-partner.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace tax / invoice mapping for co-sell

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — GreenPeak is excited to move into a co-sell listing on AWS and potentially GCP. Before we finalize listing entity details, procurement asked for a clear mapping of who will invoice them and what tax paperwork is needed. A few specific asks from our finance team: 

- Will GreenPeak receive a marketplace invoice from AWS or a direct invoice from Redwood?
- If AWS invoices the end customer, what supporting docs do you need from our side (VAT, W-8/W-9, tax residency)?
- For EU customers, do you handle reverse-charge / VAT reporting or does the marketplace do that?

We can provide a signed W-8BEN-E or W-9 depending on what you need. We also have a VAT registration certificate (EU). Can you confirm the exact filenames and a point of contact on your side?

Attached is an internal PO template they asked us to use (they said they need the vendor tax ID to match invoices).

Appreciate a short checklist we can give procurement so they can approve the co-sell listing.

Best,
Emma Lopez
Head of Procurement
GreenPeak Solutions
Attachment: GPK_PO_template.docx (docx)

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@greenpeak.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace tax / invoice mapping for co-sell

Hi Emma — great question and an easy checklist to produce. High level: marketplace billing varies by cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) and by region; we typically see two patterns: marketplace-billed (cloud invoices customer; vendor receives payout and gets a remittance report) or vendor-billed (vendor issues invoice directly to customer, marketplace collects fees separately). For co-sell on AWS we usually default to AWS-billed for SaaS listings, which means: 

- End customer receives the invoice from AWS (they can see line items including Redwood as the vendor).
- Redwood receives a payout + a remittance file from AWS; we do NOT issue the customer-facing invoice in that flow.
- Tax collection (VAT/GST) depends on the buyer region and AWS policy; in some EU scenarios AWS will collect VAT, in others the buyer self-assesses (reverse-charge).

For your checklist, please provide: 
1) Official legal billing entity name you want displayed on the listing (exact spelling)
2) Billing address and VAT number (for EU) or US tax ID (EIN)
3) Signed W-8BEN-E if GreenPeak is non-US, or W-9 if US entity (we need the PDF copy)
4) Any reseller or entity-level PO requirements (PO number format, billing contact)

I attached our short marketplace tax guide that lists common flows per cloud and example invoice screenshots. One note: if GreenPeak requires Redwood to issue the invoice directly (vendor-billed), we need to confirm that with the marketplace partner team and that will change payment timing and possibly require a marketplace invoice split agreement.

Next steps: can you share the legal entity name + VAT/W-8/W-9? I’ll loop in AWS account rep if we need vendor-billed mapping.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-marketplace-tax-guide.pdf (pdf)

- Does Redwood want to default to AWS-billed for this listing? Pros: simpler for buyer; Redwood receives consolidated payout. Cons: some customers prefer vendor invoice for accounting reasons.
- If vendor-billed is required, who on our finance side owns the invoice issuance and how long is our typical payment window (Net 30/45)?
- Karthik: for EU reverse-charge scenarios, do we need any specific language on our side or just the buyer's VAT + our EU VAT? Also confirm whether we should request the buyer to include "reverse charge" on the PO.

Deal: RDW-5421-GPK (HubSpot link below). I think we should ask AWS rep (Liam) to confirm whether they will collect VAT for the buyer country or pass-through. If AWS collects VAT, GreenPeak only needs proof of VAT registration for reconciliation.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/5421

Thanks — I’ll hold off replying to procurement until we align here.

Subject: Re: Marketplace nexus / invoicing handshake for GreenPeak co-sell

Hi Emma — thanks for the fast follow. Summary and concrete next steps below so procurement has a checklist they can sign off on: 

Checklist for GreenPeak procurement (what we need from you):
1) Confirm the legal billing entity to appear on the listing: exactly how should it read (legal name + DBA if any).
2) Provide a PDF of W-8BEN-E (for non-US) or W-9 (for US) + VAT registration certificate (if EU). Filename(s) are fine — we have attached what we expect: greenpeak-w8ben-e-signed.pdf.
3) Confirm whether GreenPeak requires a vendor-issued invoice (Redwood) vs marketplace-issued (AWS/GCP). If vendor-issued, state required payment terms and PO routing instructions.
4) If EU reverse-charge is intended, ask procurement to add the phrase "reverse charge" on the PO and include the buyer VAT number. Our finance team will still require a copy of the PO for reconciliation.

What Redwood/marketplace will do: 
- For AWS-billed (default): AWS will invoice the buyer and collect taxes where required. Redwood will receive remittance + payout and will provide remittance reports on request. 
- For vendor-billed (requested): Redwood will sequentially issue the invoice to the buyer; we will need a marketplace agreement amendment. This typically adds 7–10 business days to onboarding while legal and marketplace ops approve.

Action items: 
- Emma: please upload the signed tax form and VAT certificate to the DocuSign link or reply here with the files.
- Liam (AWS): can you confirm whether AWS will collect VAT in this buyer country (Spain) for this SKU? If yes, we can mark the listing as AWS-billed and procurement should receive AWS invoice.
- Vanessa / Karthik: finance note — if vendor-billed is requested we should prepare a short addendum outlining payment terms and refund/credit flow.

Thanks all — I’ll track this in HubSpot (RDW-5421-GPK) and update once we have the AWS confirmation.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
